items.title: The BHMV root-of-unity skein parameter

references.title: C. Blanchet, N. Habegger, G. Masbaum, and P. Vogel, Topological Quantum Field Theories Derived from the Kauffman Bracket, Topology 34 (1995), §§1–3
Louis H. Kauffman and Sostenes L. Lins, Temperley-Lieb Recoupling Theory and Invariants of 3-Manifolds, Chapters 2–3
Joshua Chen, The Temperley-Lieb Categories and Skein Modules, §§2.1 and 5.1–5.4

items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the parameter and finite label set are specified from one fixed root of unity.
items.statement:
Fix an even integer $p\ge4$ and a primitive $2p$-th root of unity $A\in\mathbb C$. Put

$$\zeta=A^2,\qquad q=-\zeta,\qquad r=p/2,\qquad \delta=-A^2-A^{-2}=q+q^{-1}.$$

The coefficient field after specialization is $\mathbb C$, and the Kauffman bracket loop coefficient is $\delta$ in the framed-link relation $[L\sqcup O]=\delta[L]$. Define the quantum integers by $[0]=0$, $[1]=1$, and $[j+1]=\delta[j]-[j-1]$ for $j\ge1$. Since $q^2=A^4$ has order $r\ge2$, these quantum integers also satisfy

$$[j]=\frac{q^j-q^{-j}}{q-q^{-1}}=(-1)^{j-1}\frac{A^{2j}-A^{-2j}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.$$

The BHMV simple-label convention is the finite set

$$\mathcal J_p=\{0,1,\ldots,r-2\}.$$

The pivotal loop and coefficient conventions throughout this page are the displayed $\delta$ and $\mathbb C$; no zero quantum integer is inverted.

items.title: Jones–Wenzl projectors exist up to the first zero quantum integer

references.title: Louis H. Kauffman and Sostenes L. Lins, Temperley-Lieb Recoupling Theory and Invariants of 3-Manifolds, Chapter 3
C. Blanchet, N. Habegger, G. Masbaum, and P. Vogel, Topological Quantum Field Theories Derived from the Kauffman Bracket, §3

items.axiom_use: Choice-free: all calculations are finite Laurent-polynomial and complex-field computations.
items.statement: Let $p\ge4$ be even, let $A$ be a primitive $2p$-th root of unity, and use the quantum integers and Temperley–Lieb loop value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ specified above. Write $r=p/2$. The standard Jones–Wenzl recursion defines nonzero idempotents $p_n$ for $0\le n\le r-1$; their unnormalized closure traces are $[n+1]$. In particular, $p_{r-1}$ has trace zero and is negligible, while the next standard recursive formula for $p_r$ is undefined because its denominator is $[r]=0$. This statement concerns that recursion and does not assert that no differently constructed normalized idempotent can exist at rank $r$.

items.title: Semisimplified Temperley–Lieb quotient at the BHMV root

references.title: C. Blanchet, N. Habegger, G. Masbaum, and P. Vogel, Topological Quantum Field Theories Derived from the Kauffman Bracket, Topology 34 (1995), §§3–4
Razvan Gelca, Topological Quantum Field Theory with Corners Based on the Kauffman Bracket, §§2–4

items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the quotient, finite additive envelope, and idempotent completion are algebraic constructions.
items.statement: Fix an even integer $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A\in\mathbb C$, $r=p/2$, and loop value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. Let $\mathcal T_\delta$ be the complex Temperley–Lieb diagram category with objects the nonnegative integers and morphisms finite linear combinations of perfect matchings of bottom and top boundary points with no intersecting arcs. Compose by stacking and remove each closed component with factor $\delta$. Define $\mathcal N_\delta(m,n)$ to be the subspace of morphisms $f:m\to n$ such that $\operatorname{Tr}_m(g\circ f)=0$ for every reverse morphism $g:n\to m$, where $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the unnormalized diagram-closure trace. Form the quotient category with the same objects and morphism spaces $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\delta}(m,n)/\mathcal N_\delta(m,n)$. Its additive envelope adjoins finite formal direct sums, with matrix morphisms and matrix composition. Its idempotent completion adjoins objects $(X,e)$ for idempotents $e\in\operatorname{End}(X)$ with $e^2=e$, and morphisms $(X,e)\to(Y,f)$ are morphisms $a:X\to Y$ satisfying $a=fae$. Juxtaposition, planar cup-cap duality, and the induced trace descend to this completed quotient. This definition makes no assertion that it is semisimple, that its simple objects have a specified label set, or that any braid, twist, or modularity identities hold.

items.title: Root Jones–Wenzl recursion and its negligible ideal

references.title: Joshua Chen, The Temperley-Lieb Categories and Skein Modules, §§5.1–5.4
Louis H. Kauffman and Sostenes L. Lins, Temperley-Lieb Recoupling Theory and Invariants of 3-Manifolds, Chapters 3–7

items.axiom_use: Choice-free: only finite Temperley–Lieb diagrams and linear algebra over C are used.
items.statement: Fix even $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A$, and $r=p/2$. In the Temperley–Lieb diagram category over $\mathbb C$ with loop value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, call $f:m\to n$ negligible when $\operatorname{Tr}_m(g\circ f)=0$ for every reverse morphism $g:n\to m$, where $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the unnormalized diagram-closure trace. A tensor ideal is a family of linear subspaces of the morphism spaces closed under composition on either side and tensor product on either side by arbitrary morphisms. The negligible morphisms form a tensor ideal. This ideal is generated, as a tensor ideal, by the Jones–Wenzl projector $p_{r-1}$, defined by the standard recursion through its first zero quantum integer; in particular the quotient has precisely the surviving projector labels $0,\ldots,r-2$.

items.axiom_use: Choice-free: all root, fusion, parity, and finite-sine calculations are finite algebraic arguments.
items.statement:
Let $p\ge4$ be even, $A\in\mathbb C$ a primitive $2p$-th root, and $r=p/2$. In the BHMV Temperley–Lieb quotient with loop value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ and planar pivotal trace, the complete simple-label set is $\{0,1,\ldots,r-2\}$, represented by the surviving Jones–Wenzl projectors $p_a$ obtained from the standard recursion using unit denominators $[2],\ldots,[a]$. Every simple is self-dual. Its fusion multiplicities are

$$N_{ab}^{c}=1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad |a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,\,2r-4-a-b) \ \text{and }a+b+c\text{ is even},$$

and are zero otherwise. With the BHMV overcrossing map $c_i=A1_i+A^{-1}U_i$, where $U_i$ is the cup-cap generator, the full-framing ribbon structure has planar quantum dimensions $d_a=[a+1]$ and simple-object twists $\theta_a=(-1)^aA^{a(a+2)}$. Here the quantum integers use the fixed BHMV recurrence. The unnormalized Hopf-link matrix, whose $(a,b)$ entry is the pivotal trace of the double braiding on $p_a\otimes p_b$, is nondegenerate. Here modular means that this finite semisimple ribbon category has an invertible unnormalized Hopf-link matrix.

items.title: Weighted Lagrangian extension and root anomaly data

references.title: C. Blanchet, N. Habegger, G. Masbaum, and P. Vogel, Topological Quantum Field Theories Derived from the Kauffman Bracket, §§1–2 and Appendix B

items.axiom_use: Full AC is a declared prerequisite of the weighted Lagrangian bordism interface; choosing the displayed roots for one fixed p and A is a finite pointwise choice, with no familywise choice used in this definition.
items.statement:
For the fixed root parameter, let $\mathcal C_p$ denote the semisimplified Temperley–Lieb category with labels $0,\ldots,r-2$, pivotal dimensions $d_j=[j+1]$, and Hopf-link data inherited from the Kauffman bracket. Put $\mathcal D_p^2=\sum_{j=0}^{r-2}d_j^2$ and choose $\mathcal D_p\in\mathbb C$ with that square. Choose $\kappa\in\mathbb C$ satisfying $\kappa^6=A^{-6-(p+1)p/2}$. The root-specific extended data are the weighted Lagrangian ribbon bordisms whose objects are closed oriented labeled surfaces with a Lagrangian subspace of real first homology and whose morphisms are collared oriented labeled ribbon bordisms with integer weights. If $M_1:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ and $M_2:\Sigma_1\to\Sigma_2$ have relations $\Lambda_{M_1},\Lambda_{M_2}$ and boundary Lagrangians $\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2$, define

$$K_1=\Lambda_{M_1}(\lambda_0),\qquad K_0=\lambda_1,\qquad K_2=\Lambda_{M_2}^{\,t}(\lambda_2), \qquad n(M_2\circ M_1)=n_2+n_1+\mu(K_1,K_0,K_2),$$

using the Wall-signature Maslov convention. The category composition, units, and anomaly weight are those specified by this formula and the weighted Lagrangian bordism definition; no ordinary oriented anomaly-free functor is part of this Definition.

items.axiom_use: Choice-free in the finite color calculations; full AC is carried separately by the surgery-presentation theorem that consumes this result.
items.statement: Fix even $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A$, the BHMV semisimplified category, and its quantum dimensions $d_j$ and twists $\theta_j$ for $0\le j\le r-2$. Put $\Omega_p=\sum_{j=0}^{r-2}d_jp_j$, $\Delta_+=\sum_jd_j^2\theta_j$, and $\Delta_-=\sum_jd_j^2\theta_j^{-1}$. The Statement asserts that both $\Delta_+$ and $\Delta_-$ are nonzero. For a finite integral framed link $L$ in the oriented three-sphere, color each surgery component by $\Omega_p$ and normalize the bracket evaluation by $\Delta_+^{b_+(L)}\Delta_-^{b_-(L)}$, where $b_\pm(L)$ are the positive and negative indices of the framing matrix. With the stated BHMV root and weighted anomaly convention, the resulting value is unchanged under framed isotopy, handle slides, and addition or deletion of a split $\pm1$-framed unknot.

items.axiom_use: Full AC is retained through the surgery-presentation supplier used to define the closed pairing invariant.
items.statement:
Assume full AC for the surgery-presentation and universal-construction inputs below. Fix an even integer $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A\in\mathbb C$, put $r=p/2$ and $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, and use the selected BHMV sixth root $\kappa$ satisfying $\kappa^6=A^{-6-(p+1)p/2}$. Fix a closed oriented marked surface $\Sigma$ with its Lagrangian and weighted anomaly data. Let $I_\Sigma$ be the finite union of its marked ribbon-end bands, with each band labeled by its specified simple object $a_j\in\{0,\ldots,r-2\}$. Fix a marked handlebody $H$ with boundary $\Sigma$ and a complementary marked handlebody $H'$ so that their oriented gluing is the standard $S^3$; the boundary bands on $H$ and $H'$ are identified by the marking, with labels dualized on the oppositely oriented side.

For a banded boundary link $I$ in $\partial H$, let $\mathcal K_A(H;I)$ be the complex specialization of the relative Jones–Kauffman skein module generated by framed banded links in $H$ meeting $\partial H$ transversely in exactly $I$, modulo framed isotopy fixed on $\partial H$ and the following local relations in interior balls. In a chart where the over-strand runs southwest to northeast and the under-strand northwest to southeast, let $L_A$ join the two left endpoints and the two right endpoints, and let $L_B$ join the top endpoints and the bottom endpoints, with blackboard framing. Impose $[L_\times]=A[L_A]+A^{-1}[L_B]$. If $O$ is a zero-framed trivial circle bounding a disk disjoint from the rest of the link, impose $[L\sqcup O]=\delta[L]$. The empty link is allowed.

Let $\widetilde I_\Sigma$ be the boundary link obtained by replacing each band $I_j$ by $a_j$ parallel bands, deleting it when $a_j=0$. On $\mathcal K_A(H;\widetilde I_\Sigma)$, the identity-coefficient Jones–Wenzl projector $p_{a_j}$ acts on the corresponding parallel strands in a boundary collar. Define the colored relative skein module by $\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)=P_{\mathbf a}\mathcal K_A(H;\widetilde I_\Sigma)$, where $P_{\mathbf a}$ is the product of these mutually disjoint boundary projectors. Every denominator in these projectors is among $[2],\ldots,[a_j]$, which are nonzero because $a_j\le r-2$. When $I_\Sigma$ is empty, this is the ordinary closed-link module $\mathcal K_A(H)$.

For $x\in\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)$ and $y\in\mathcal K_A(H';I_\Sigma,\mathbf a^*)$, glue their matching boundary bands and idempotents. This gives a closed colored ribbon graph $\Gamma$ in the standard $S^3$. Define the handlebody pairing by $B_\Sigma(x,y)=Z_p(S^3,\Gamma,w)$, using the normalized root surgery evaluation and the weight $w$ prescribed by the fixed Lagrangian data. This is the BHMV sesquilinear pairing: it is linear in $x$ and conjugate-linear in $y$ for the coefficient involution $A\mapsto A^{-1}$, $\kappa\mapsto\kappa^{-1}$. Define

$$\operatorname{Rad}(B_\Sigma)=\{x\in\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a):B_\Sigma(x,y)=0\text{ for every }y\in\mathcal K_A(H';I_\Sigma,\mathbf a^*)\}, \qquad V_p(\Sigma)=\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)/\operatorname{Rad}(B_\Sigma).$$

This is the radical-quotient handlebody state-space construction for the specified marking and anomaly data. Independence of the marking, finite generation, nondegeneracy, and the gluing maps are separate mathematical obligations.

**External normalization input.** In this Definition the closed marked evaluation is the BHMV TQFT normalization, not merely the raw signature-normalized closed invariant $\theta_p$ of the Kirby lemma. BHMV §2 pp.897–898 and Gilmer–Masbaum §11 pp.23–25 give
$$Z_p(M,\Gamma,w)=\eta^{b_0(M)+b_1(M)}(\kappa^3)^w\theta_p(M,\Gamma),\qquad \Delta_\pm=\eta^{-1}\kappa^{\pm3}.$$
Let $g_p=\frac12\sum_{m=1}^{2p}(-1)^mA^{m^2}$, and let the bar denote the BHMV involution $A\mapsto A^{-1}$, $\kappa\mapsto\kappa^{-1}$. The normalizing scalar is $\eta=(A\kappa)^3(A^2-A^{-2})p^{-1}\overline{g_p}\in\mathbb C^\times$. Thus $Z_p(S^3,\varnothing,0)=\eta$ and $Z_p(S^2\times S^1,\varnothing,0)=1$. These nonzero normalizations and the registered Wall-sign weight are part of the pairing. BHMV Proposition 1.9, p. 891, applies to a general prescribed banded boundary link $I$: the map from the relative skein module to the universal state space is surjective and its kernel is the left radical of the complementary pairing. For colored boundary bands, BHMV §§4.5–4.8 realize each color by the corresponding parallel cable and Jones–Wenzl projector. BHMV Theorem 4.11, p. 909, states that admissibly colored relative spines whose boundary is the prescribed colored link form an orthogonal basis. The selected $\kappa$ remains a sixth root, with one weight step acting by its cube. The source is used at these located statements and constructions, not as a claimed locally reconstructed universal-construction proof.

**Source hypotheses for this identification.** The normalized BHMV closed invariant is multiplicative and involutive, so BHMV Proposition 1.1 gives its cobordism-generated quantization functor at this fixed root; extend its coefficients to $\mathbb C$ as stated above. BHMV Theorem 1.7 supplies both hypotheses needed for Proposition 1.9: its Kauffman bracket relations let that proposition replace the free relative bordism module by the specialized relative skein module, and its surgery axioms give the surjectivity and radical-kernel description. BHMV's colored expansion in §§4.5–4.8 transports the same construction to the boundary projectors defining $\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)$. The corresponding weighted Lagrangian version is the BHMV skein TQFT with integral weights and Lagrangians in place of $p_1$-structures, as described by Gilmer–Masbaum in §11; their one-weight multiplier is matched to the selected BHMV sixth root by $\kappa_{\mathrm{GM}}=\kappa^3$. In that section Lemma 11.1 states the weighted surgery axiom and Remark 11.3 applies it to the handlebody skein presentation; the source refers the Lemma 11.1 proof to the BHMV argument rather than repeating it. These are imported source inputs, not a locally reconstructed proof, and they do not add another quotient or change the state-space interface.

items.axiom_use: Finite choice only is needed for a fixed finite spine; full AC is inherited from the declared state-space/surgery interface.
items.statement: Let $(H,I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)$ be a marked handlebody with prescribed boundary bands $I_\Sigma$ and boundary labels $\mathbf a$. Fix a finite banded relative spine $G\subset H$, meaning a banded graph whose degree-one boundary vertices give exactly $I_\Sigma$, whose interior vertices have degree two or three, and whose regular neighborhood is $H$; for the unmarked $3$-ball, the empty graph is allowed. Let each edge carry a label in $\{0,\ldots,r-2\}$, with every boundary half-edge on a band $I_j$ labeled by its prescribed color $a_j$. Call a labeling admissible when labels agree across every interior $2$-valent vertex and the three labels at each interior trivalent vertex satisfy the root fusion rule. In the radical-quotient state space $V_p(\Sigma)$, the states represented by admissibly colored relative spines span, and the set of such labelings is finite. This statement asserts spanning, not linear independence.
